page: Amazon Web Services m5d.4xlarge is a general-purpose, Nitro-based virtual server designed for workloads that demand balanced compute, memory, and fast local NVMe storage. Powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8259CL processor, this x86_64 instance provides 16 vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core operating at 3.1 GHz. The hardware architecture features 35 MB of L3 cache, along with AVX-512 and AES instruction set extensions. System memory consists of 64.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 4:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU.

Integrated hardware includes 600 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD instance storage and a 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance features no GPU accelerators. Direct-attached NVMe storage delivers low-latency scratch space and high-throughput temporary caching directly at the hypervisor level, reducing dependence on network-attached block devices for transient reads and writes.

Empirical benchmarks reflect consistent mid-tier performance across multi-threaded computational workloads, alongside modest single-thread capabilities. The instance achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 6817.0, a PassMark CPU score of 14405.52, and 13,469.19 in stress-ng multi-core testing, positioning it squarely in the middle 50% of comparable servers. In contrast, Geekbench single-core (1078.0) and single-threaded gzip compression (22.49 GB/sec) scored in the bottom 25%, highlighting limited per-thread processing efficiency compared to newer architecture nodes.

Memory and caching tests confirm solid general-purpose throughput, reaching 778.54 GB/sec for cached 16 KB read operations, 89.01 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, and 13.68 million Redis SET operations per second. Web throughput reached 11.87 GB/sec. Qualitatively, the combination of 16 vCPUs, 64 GB RAM, and bundled local NVMe storage offers balanced resource density and operational cost efficiency for transactional applications, clustered build agents, staging databases, and cache layers that require low-latency scratch capacity.

The primary operational tradeoff centers on single-core execution speed and the ephemeral nature of instance store volumes. Because local NVMe storage does not persist beyond instance termination, applications must manage data durability externally. Amazon Web Services m5d.4xlarge is best suited for relational and key-value database caching, containerized web application clusters, intermediate ETL processing, and continuous integration pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services m5d.4xlarge is a balanced general-purpose instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor on the AWS Nitro System. Featuring 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores at 3.1 GHz, the x86_64 server is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR4 RAM, 600 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, and 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark data shows standard mid-tier performance across multi-threaded operations, including a PassMark CPU score of 14405.52 and 13.68 million Redis SET operations per second, counterbalanced by modest single-threaded throughput. With its 4:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio and direct-attached storage, the instance provides cost-effective resource density for caching servers, container clusters, data manipulation pipelines, and mid-tier transactional databases.
